title: Introduce epochal warmset allocator and utilization-signal throttler
author: Priya Mahadevan
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets were seeing disproportionate cold tail latency during cross-tenant burst startup events. Existing warm-pool heuristics pre-warm capacity per-cluster without coordinating epochs, which leads to both over-provisioning and missed warm hits when many tenants spike simultaneously. This PR introduces an "epochal warmset allocator": an epoch-based warm pool assignment system that batches warm allocations into short, aligned epochs and spreads warmset churn across clusters to reduce peak allocation pressure. In parallel, this PR adds a utilization-signal throttler that consumes a smoothed utilization estimate (multi-window low-pass) to apply temporary soft throttles to non-critical routes during transient overloads rather than triggering hard evictions.

Design summary: The epochal warmset allocator groups warm set requests into configurable epochs (default 30s). During each epoch the allocator computes a global warmset plan using tenant-weight and recent request locality, then issues pre-warm tokens to selected pool nodes using a staggered rollout to avoid spikes. The allocator keeps an epoch history ring buffer to estimate churn and hit-rate improvements.

The utilization-signal throttler subscribes to per-pool utilization rollups (1s/10s/60s windows), computes a weighted low-pass composite, and exposes a soft-throttle score for routes. Soft-throttle scores translate to probabilistic admission reductions and graceful response degradation (e.g., route-level concurrency hints) rather than immediate drops. Throttling is reversible and decays automatically when utilization returns below target thresholds.

What changed (single-string checklist): - Implement epochal allocator core logic and config flags; - Add warmset planner HTTP/gRPC endpoint for diagnostic dumps; - Wire allocator to Dedicated controller and to the warm pool reconciler; - Add utilization-signal aggregator and throttler hook in serving runtime; - New metrics: warmset_epoch_prep_time_seconds, warmset_hit_rate_by_epoch, util_composite_score, route_soft_throttle_probability; - Unit tests for planner heuristics and throttler scoring; - Integration test (simulated multi-tenant spike) in benchmark-lab harness; - Documentation: design doc and operator runbook with rollout plan.

Commits summary: 1) epochal-warmset: initial allocator skeleton and config (Priya); 2) warmset-planner: planner algorithm + deterministic unit tests (Priya); 3) throttler: util aggregator and throttling policy (Marco Chen); 4) integ: benchmark-lab scenario and results (Ana Rodriguez); 5) docs: runbook and operator flags (Priya).

Files touched (high-level): - services/dedicated/allocator/epochal_allocator.go - services/dedicated/allocator/planner_test.go - services/dedicated/api/warmset_debug.go - runtime/throttler/util_aggregator.go - runtime/throttler/soft_throttle_policy.go - telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml - benchmark-lab/scenarios/epochal-warmset-spike.yaml - docs/operators/epochal-warmset.md - CHANGELOG.md

Testing and CI: Local unit/integration passes; benchmark-lab run shows 42% reduction in cold-start tail p99 for the simulated tenant mix while increasing average warm-pool utilization by 12%. CI initially hit a flake in planner_test.go due to time-based nondeterminism; fixed by injecting a deterministic epoch clock and re-running. All checks green on final run.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged by default off; staged rollout to Dedicated clusters in three phases: canary (1 cluster), regional (10% capacity), global (100%). Operator flag to control epoch length and throttler sensitivity. Observability dashboard added under Console -> Dedicated -> Warmset to track hit-rate and throttle signals. Kill switch: disable allocator and throttle by flipping feature flags and reconciling warm pools.

Related work and references: Linear ENG-1459 (warm-pool refactor), ENG-1608 (route-level soft-fallbacks). Related PRs: benchmark-lab scenario updates (was required to validate behavior). Jira SUP-1182 tracked customer incident that motivated this change.

Notes: No breaking API changes. Config knobs default to conservative values. See docs/operators/epochal-warmset.md for operational knobs and troubleshooting steps.
